body: Just source it and work directly with `$DISTRIB_ID`?

I pointed you towards neofetch for a good reason :upside_down_face: Here is how they do it:
```bash
            elif [[ -f /etc/os-release || \
                    -f /usr/lib/os-release || \
                    -f /etc/openwrt_release || \
                    -f /etc/lsb-release ]]; then

                # Source the os-release file
                for file in /etc/lsb-release /usr/lib/os-release \
                            /etc/os-release  /etc/openwrt_release; do
                    source "$file" && break
                done

                # Format the distro name.
                case $distro_shorthand in
                    on)   distro="${NAME:-${DISTRIB_ID}} ${VERSION_ID:-${DISTRIB_RELEASE}}" ;;
                    tiny) distro="${NAME:-${DISTRIB_ID:-${TAILS_PRODUCT_NAME}}}" ;;
                    off)  distro="${PRETTY_NAME:-${DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION}} ${UBUNTU_CODENAME}" ;;
                esac
```
Also, you're gonna need lowercase it because here is what I get on Linux Mint 19.2:
```sh
# from /etc/lsb-release
DISTRIB_ID=LinuxMint

# from /etc/os-release
ID=linuxmint
```
And you can extend that (allow)list with Linux Mint because it is fairly popular Ubuntu derivate :wink:
I think I prefer the old check https://github.com/starship/starship/commit/2e14d1af5a3b90aedab39180e0851e8f945b9f55

```sh
if [ "$platform" = "linux" ] && ldd /bin/sh | grep -iq musl; then
  platform=unknown-linux-musl
fi
```
so, something like the old check, but flipping it to detect glibc, would be ideal if we also add a check for the glibc version that works in a cross platform way, right?

this seems to work. I'll rework the PR to use it
```
$ ldd --version | head -n1 | sed -e 's/ldd (GNU libc) //'
2.28
```

(first detecting if the string contains GNU libc, of course)

You can simplify it by replacing `head` plus `sed` combo with `awk`:
```sh
ldd --version | awk 'NR==1 { print $NF }'
# or invoking /usr/lib/libc.so.6 directly
/usr/lib/libc.so.6 | awk 'NR==1 { gsub(/\.$/,""); print $NF }'
```

@vladimyr good point! I also want to check if the string contain 'GNU libc' though, so might as well reuse that string for both the check and to extract the version (see updated commit). I can use `awk` if that's preferable

Well, in that case you can use following checks:
```sh
ldd --version | awk '/GNU libc/ { print $NF }'
# or invoking /usr/lib/libc.so.6 directly
/usr/lib/libc.so.6 | awk '/GNU libc/ { gsub(/\.$/,""); print $NF }'
```

> I can use `awk` if that's preferable

The sole reason why I prefer `awk` here is to minimize calls to external binaries.

$ ldd --version

This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
Written by Roland McGrath and Ulrich Drepper.

# arch

Copyright (C) 2021 Free Software Foundation, Inc.

+      # default to the statically compiled musl bins on linux

+        glibc_version=$(echo "${ldd_verstr}" | sed -e "s/^${ldd_glibc_prefix}//")
+        # on installations with a new enough glibc, use the dynamically compiled binary

+        #
+        # then use https://gist.github.com/fasterthanlime/17e002a8f5e0f189861c with
+        # `MAX_VER` set to the version from earlier e.g. GLIBC_2.33 => 2.33
+        min_version="2.18"
+        if [ "${glibc_version}" > "${min_version}" ] \
body:
This is redirection unless escaped: `\>` :warning: 
Even then it is lexical comparison between strings rather than numerical one:
```sh
~ $ [ 3.22 \> 3.3 ] && echo 'true' || echo 'false'
false
```
Debugging leftovers I guess? :upside_down_face:

I guess the cleanest way is to split based on dot and explicitly compare the parts as integers
